review.verdict: Casting and palette are fine, but the dial clips outside the safe area, the leak and sweep metaphors are too faint/disconnected to read quickly, and the right side feels like a crowded stack rather than one clear beat — average comes in under the bar.
revisionNotes: Dial is clipped at the right edge/safe area (lint: x 924-1064, y 555-695) — scale it to ~0.85 and shift left-third within the person's reach so it isn't cut off.
The leak metaphor is too subtle: the crack/confetti bits floating above the bubble read as a random squiggle, not a spray of secrets — scale them up and route them visibly toward the network shape.
Right side stacks pile, dial, SLOP tag, and bin in a disconnected vertical column — add a short swept-motion line or arrow from the pile toward the bin so the 'sweeping away' action is legible.

Brief calls for a thin divider between the two vignettes; currently there's no visual separation, so the leak story and the dial/bin story blur into one busy scene — add a vertical rule or clearer gap at the midline.
The pile circles read as coins/buttons, not duplicate AI music tracks — add a small note/waveform glyph inside each circle so 'music-track icons' is recognizable.
Clean up the overlap where the person's pointing arm crosses the torso (a stray reddish sliver near the shoulder) for a crisper pose.

review.verdict: A solid two-panel concept with correct casting, but the right panel's arm/dial/bin overlap reads as a rendering glitch and muddies the 'turning the dial' action, dragging the average just under passing.
revisionNotes: Fix the overlap where the human's arm runs straight into the SLOP bin's label — shorten/angle the 'point' arm so the hand visibly lands on the dial's rim instead of merging with the bin text.
The dial component is clipped behind the human's torso and legs; move it to x≈0.64, y≈0.70 (clear of the body) and scale to 1.1 so the turning action reads.
Swap the inner glyph on the track-pile circles (currently small bar-chart bars) for a music-note shape so the pile reads unambiguously as duplicate music tracks, not generic analytics.
Scale the network/web graphic to ~1.15; at current size the thin lines read as scribbles until you look closely, weakening the 'leak' destination.
Add more separation between the dial-turn gesture and the sweep-into-bin dashed line so the two actions (turning away vs. sweeping) don't visually collapse into one stroke.

review.verdict: Left vignette lands cleanly, but the divider literally cuts through the human figure and the dial floats disconnected from the pointing hand, muddying the right-side metaphor and the overall polish — this narrowly fails the bar today.
revisionNotes: Move the "human" anchor off the divider: shift x from 0.5 to ~0.56 so the thin vertical divider line doesn't pierce straight through the figure's head and torso — currently the line visibly bisects the body, a polish bug.

Pull the "dial" closer to the human's pointing hand (e.g. anchor it near x=0.56, y=0.75) and scale it to ~1.3 so the hand reads as touching/turning it, instead of floating near the arm as an unrelated clock shape.
Rotate the dial's needle to point away from the trackflow pile (toward the left, away from x=0.85) so "turning the dial away from the pile" reads in under 3 seconds without close inspection.
Tighten the trackflow pile into a denser, more obviously identical grid of note-circles (reduce scatter) so "duplicate AI slop tracks" is legible at a glance.

This split-card-with-vertical-divider plus person/robot pairing is close in structure to recent cards (the open-door/high-bar and costs-more/costs-less sloppers) — try an angled or torn divider, or a top/bottom split, to differentiate the layout next time.
Left vignette (cracked SHARE bubble spilling papers into the network) reads clearly and can stay as-is.
